name: Small bowel adenocarcinoma

meta.title: Small bowel adenocarcinoma in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Small bowel adenocarcinoma (duodenal, jejunal, ileal), adult
meta.population: Adults with histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the small intestine, across the resected curative-intent setting and the advanced (unresectable, metastatic, or recurrent) setting. The other small-intestine histologies are excluded and hard-rerouted: gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumours, gastrointestinal stromal tumour, and small-bowel lymphoma each have their own guideline chapter, their own arm family, and their own catalog row. Ampullary adenocarcinoma is out of scope as a primary site, and where a cited anchor enrolled ampullary patients that is recorded on the card.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for a rare cancer whose defining feature is that almost nothing about it has been randomised. It shows how an in silico engine gates, models, and ranks decisions across the small bowel adenocarcinoma journey - the histology gate that decides whether this trainer applies at all, AJCC 8th-edition staging and the high-risk features that drive the adjuvant question, the mismatch-repair result that reroutes advanced disease from chemotherapy to immunotherapy, and the later-line menu - for clinicians, patients, and caregivers. The teaching spine is evidentiary h…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO Classification of Digestive System Tumours; AJCC 8th edition TNM for small intestine carcinoma (N1 = 1-2 nodes, N2 = >=3 nodes)

stages.label: Confirm the histology
stages.question: Is this small bowel adenocarcinoma - and is it the disease this trainer covers?
stages.decision: Confirm adenocarcinoma histology before anything else; reroute neuroendocrine, GIST, and lymphoma.

stages.label: Stage, margins, and risk features
stages.question: What stage is this, was the resection complete, and which high-risk features are present?
stages.decision: Resolve AJCC 8th-edition T and N, the number of nodes examined, margin status, grade, and mismatch-repair status.

stages.label: Adjuvant decision
stages.question: After a complete resection, does this patient benefit from chemotherapy - or only from its side effects?
stages.decision: Rank the post-resection options against the risk-stratified evidence, and show which ones the evidence does not support.

stages.label: Surveillance and recurrence checkpoint
stages.question: Has the disease come back - and what does that change?
stages.decision: Read surveillance imaging; route a confirmed recurrence into the advanced-disease menu.

stages.label: Advanced disease, first line
stages.question: Unresectable or metastatic - which first-line strategy, for this biology?
stages.decision: Rank first-line arms; mismatch-repair status decides whether this is a chemotherapy or an immunotherapy conversation.

stages.label: Progression and later lines
stages.question: First line has failed - what now?
stages.decision: Rank later-line options under the sequencing rules; show what is trial-only.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which open studies fit this patient today?
stages.decision: Evaluate encodable criteria three-state: match, blocked, needs-data.

stages.label: Data readiness
stages.question: Which missing result would change the answer most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live value-of-information flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Median age at diagnosis was 63.5 years in the resected French cohort and 63 in ARCAD-NADEGE. Age enters as a cited hazard modifier, never as a hard gate; trial age ranges stay on the cards.
Patient.helpPatient: Age shifts the odds but does not by itself close any door in this trainer.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: ECOG 2 and >=3 carry cited hazard modifiers, and combination chemotherapy arms require ECOG <=2 - the same threshold the open first-line randomised trial uses for entry.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily activity is possible right now - it shifts the numbers and it opens or closes the more intensive options.

Patient.label: Predisposing condition
Patient.help: Predisposing disease was present in about one in five ARCAD-NADEGE patients and changes tumour biology, not just risk: Crohn disease clusters with ileal location and poor differentiation, Lynch syndr…
Patient.helpPatient: A pre-existing condition that raised the risk of this cancer. It can change what the tumour looks like and what tests the family may need.

Diagnostic gates.label: Histology
Diagnostic gates.help: The small intestine hosts four distinct malignancies with four unrelated arm families. Anything other than adenocarcinoma hard-reroutes out of this trainer to its own spec.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: The exact cell type decides which treatment map applies - they are genuinely different diseases in the same organ.

Diagnostic gates.label: Primary site
Diagnostic gates.help: Duodenum is the commonest primary (60.6% in ARCAD-NADEGE). Site is not a prognostic modifier here - it is a predictive one: jejunal and ileal primaries showed a significant interaction with adjuvant…
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Which part of the small bowel the cancer started in - it changes how much the after-surgery chemotherapy is expected to help.

Stage and risk.label: AJCC stage
Stage and risk.help: AJCC 8th edition. Drives the recurrence-risk prior and the survival modifiers anchored to ARCAD-NADEGE 5-year overall survival: 87.9% stage I, 78.2% stage II, 55.5% stage III, median 12.7 months at s…
Stage and risk.helpPatient: How far the cancer had spread when it was found - the strongest single driver of the numbers on these cards.

Stage and risk.label: T category
Stage and risk.help: AJCC 8th edition has no T4a/T4b split for small intestine carcinoma. T4 was an independent prognostic factor after resection (p=0.001) and is half of the high-risk definition that predicted adjuvant…
Stage and risk.helpPatient: How deeply the tumour grew through the bowel wall.

Stage and risk.label: N category
Stage and risk.help: AJCC 8th edition: N1 is 1-2 involved nodes (stage IIIA), N2 is 3 or more (stage IIIB). N2 is the other half of the high-risk stage III definition that predicted adjuvant benefit.
Stage and risk.helpPatient: How many nearby lymph nodes contained cancer cells.

Stage and risk.label: Resection status
Stage and risk.help: Curative-intent arms require a complete (R0) resection; anything less routes to the advanced-disease menu. 58.9% of ARCAD-NADEGE patients presented with localized resectable disease.
Stage and risk.helpPatient: Whether the surgery removed all visible and microscopic cancer.

Stage and risk.label: Lymph nodes examined
Stage and risk.help: Fewer than 8 nodes examined defines high-risk stage II in the analysis that drives this spec's adjuvant logic - an understaging proxy, not a biological one. It is the quiet input that can move a pati…
Stage and risk.helpPatient: How many lymph nodes the pathologist was able to check. A small number means the staging itself is less certain.

Stage and risk.label: Differentiation (grade)
Stage and risk.help: Poor differentiation was one of only two surviving prognostic factors for overall survival in resected ARCAD-NADEGE patients (p=0.047), alongside T stage.
Stage and risk.helpPatient: How abnormal the cancer cells look under the microscope.

Molecular panel.label: Mismatch repair / MSI status
Molecular panel.help: The single biggest lever in advanced disease: deficiency reroutes the menu from chemotherapy to a tissue-agnostic checkpoint-inhibitor approval. Prevalence is stage-dependent - 31.9% in stage III ver…
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A test of the tumour's DNA repair machinery. If it is broken, an immunotherapy option opens that works far better than chemotherapy for that group - it is worth waiting for.

Molecular panel.label: KRAS / RAS status
Molecular panel.help: The commonest alteration in this disease (44.0% in the NADEGE panel; 72.7% in synchronous metastatic tumours). Wild-type status opens the anti-EGFR arm - which exists here to show that it did not hel…
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A gene result that decides whether one particular add-on drug is even considered. In this cancer that add-on has not been shown to work.

Molecular panel.label: HER2 (ERBB2) status
Molecular panel.help: Positive in 7.7% of stage IV small bowel adenocarcinomas by gastric scoring criteria, and ERBB2 was altered in 7.2% of the NADEGE panel. This trainer models it as a trial-unlocking artifact rather th…
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A protein that, when present in large amounts, can open targeted drugs in other cancers. In this one it currently points toward a clinical trial rather than a standard treatment.

Molecular panel.label: Tumour mutational burden
Molecular panel.help: In ZEBRA the single confirmed response among mismatch-repair-proficient tumours correlated with high mutational burden. The TMB-high indication is an FDA accelerated approval, so the arm it opens dis…
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A count of how many mutations the tumour carries. A high count can occasionally open immunotherapy even when the repair-machinery test is normal - on early, unconfirmed evidence.

Treatment history.label: Prior platinum-based chemotherapy
Treatment history.help: Gates the later-line menu: FOLFIRI's only evidence in this disease is as second line after platinum failure, and both open refractory trials require prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum exposure.
Treatment history.helpPatient: Whether the standard first chemotherapy combination has already been tried.

On treatment.label: First-line restaging (RECIST 1.1)
On treatment.help: Read at 8-12 weeks. Response or stable disease continues the current line; progression routes to the later-line menu. Median progression-free survival on first-line chemotherapy alone was 8.0 months,…
On treatment.helpPatient: The scan a couple of months in that tells us whether the current treatment is working.

On treatment.label: Surveillance finding
On treatment.help: Post-resection surveillance imaging. A confirmed recurrence collapses the modeled recurrence-risk posterior into an observation and routes the patient to the advanced-disease state.
On treatment.helpPatient: The follow-up scans after surgery, checking whether anything has come back.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Complete resection, then surveillance
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma - resection is the only curative modality
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: surgical morbidity only; no systemic toxicity
Newly diagnosed.patient: Surgery removed the cancer, and the plan is careful watching rather than more treatment.
drugs: Segmental small-bowel resection with regional lymphadenectomy, or pancreaticoduodenectomy for duodenal primaries

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant capecitabine + oxaliplatin (CAPOX)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN option after resection; oxaliplatin-based regimens were 89.9% of adjuvant use in ARCAD-NADEGE
Newly diagnosed.evidence: retrospective, propensity/IPTW-weighted - no randomised trial has reported
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: peripheral neuropathy, hand-foot syndrome, cytopenias, diarrhoea; DPYD consideration before fluoropyrimidine
Newly diagnosed.patient: Six months of chemotherapy after surgery, aiming to kill cells too small to see - the tablets-plus-drip version.

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant FOLFOX (infusional)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: retrospective, propensity/IPTW-weighted - no head-to-head comparison with CAPOX in this disease
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: as CAPOX plus port-related risks; less hand-foot syndrome, more line care
Newly diagnosed.patient: The same six months of chemotherapy, given entirely by drip through a small implanted port instead of partly as tablets.
drugs: Implanted venous access port + ambulatory infusion pump

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant fluoropyrimidine alone
Newly diagnosed.guideline: reasonable when oxaliplatin is not tolerable; no disease-specific effect estimate verified
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: hand-foot syndrome, diarrhoea, mucositis; no neuropathy
Newly diagnosed.patient: A gentler single chemotherapy tablet after surgery, for when the two-drug combination would be too hard on the body.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always a valid choice; stated honestly here because a curative alternative exists
Newly diagnosed.patient: Full attention on feeling as well as possible, chosen with open eyes: surgery is the one treatment that can cure this, so declining it changes the outlook substantially.
drugs: Symptom-directed care, nutrition support, and obstruction management

Relapsed / recurrent.name: First-line fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin (CAPOX / FOLFOX)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN first-line backbone; the only regimen with prospective data in this disease
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase II single-arm (n=30) plus large retrospective cohort - never randomised
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: neuropathy, cytopenias, fatigue, diarrhoea; DPYD consideration before fluoropyrimidine
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The standard first combination for advanced disease - two chemotherapy drugs that shrink the cancer in about half of people.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: First-line chemotherapy + antiangiogenic (bevacizumab)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: not a guideline-established standard in this disease; strongest available comparative signal
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: retrospective IPTW cohort (n=45 treated) - hazard ratio of 0.38 from a non-randomised comparison is itself a caution
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: adds hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding and perforation risk to the chemotherapy profile - the last matters in a bowel primary
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The standard chemotherapy plus a drug that targets the tumour's blood supply. The evidence is a careful look back at real patients, not a randomised trial - the difference matters and the card keeps it visible.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: First-line chemotherapy + anti-EGFR (RAS wild-type)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: not established in this disease; shown to teach the negative result
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: retrospective, no significant difference versus chemotherapy alone (n=16 treated of 78 RAS wild-type)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: acneiform rash, hypomagnesaemia, infusion reactions - added toxicity without a demonstrated gain
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An antibody added to chemotherapy that works well in bowel cancer of the large intestine - and, when it was looked at here, did not measurably help in small bowel cancer. It is on the screen so that result is visible rather than assumed away.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pembrolizumab (mismatch-repair deficient / MSI-H)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA tissue-agnostic approval for unresectable/metastatic MSI-H or dMMR solid tumours after prior treatment
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase II basket trial in a previously treated population; first-line use in this disease is extrapolation, and the card says so
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: immune-related adverse events; treatment-related grade 3-5 events in 14.6% of the KEYNOTE-158 cohort
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An immunotherapy drip for tumours whose DNA repair machinery is broken. For that group it works far better than chemotherapy, and sometimes shrinks the cancer enough to make surgery possible again.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pembrolizumab (TMB-high, mismatch-repair proficient)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA accelerated approval for TMB-H solid tumours after prior treatment; no disease-specific efficacy anchor
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase II that missed its primary endpoint; subgroup signal of n=1 confirmed response
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: immune-related adverse events; grade >=3 events in 63% of ZEBRA participants
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The same immunotherapy, tried when the repair-machinery test is normal but the tumour carries an unusually high number of mutations. The trial that tested this in small bowel cancer did not meet its goal - one person in forty responded - so this is a considered gamble, described as one.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Second-line FOLFIRI (after platinum failure)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN option after platinum failure; the only second-line regimen with disease-specific data
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A different chemotherapy combination after the first one stops working. It holds the cancer steady in about half of people, usually for a few months.
drugs: Implanted venous access port + ambulatory infusion pump

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always an option; integrated palliative care alongside any arm
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: focused on symptom relief; obstruction and nutrition support continue
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Full attention on comfort, appetite, and time that feels like your own, without anti-cancer drugs.
drugs: Symptom-directed care, nutrition support, and obstruction management

honesty: Registry wins for status; the peer-reviewed paper wins for numbers; both are logged.

No arm in this spec rests on a randomised controlled trial conducted in small bowel adenocarcinoma. Every advanced-disease card states its design and its sample size, and the advanced screen carries that sentence as a b…

BALLAD/PRODIGE 33 is rendered with its actual registry state - Unknown, last updated 2015 - because the adjuvant recommendation this trainer models exists only because that randomisation never delivered.

Adjuvant benefit is claimed only where it was demonstrated: high-risk stage II (T4 and/or fewer than 8 nodes examined) and high-risk stage III (T4 and/or N2). Low-risk cards state that no significant benefit was shown a…
The resection-alone baseline discloses that its cohort figure includes patients who received adjuvant chemotherapy, so it is not a pure observation arm.
The anti-EGFR card leads with the null result in RAS wild-type patients, not with the antiangiogenic result from the same analysis.
The TMB-high pembrolizumab card leads with ZEBRA's missed primary endpoint (ORR 8%, 95% CI 2-20, against a 30% target) and states that its FDA indication is an accelerated approval.
The dMMR pembrolizumab card records that KEYNOTE-158 enrolled previously treated patients across 27 tumour types and that the small-bowel subgroup size is not stated in the verified abstract.
Values labeled 'teaching approximation' are derived from verified anchors by a stated arithmetic step, or are explicitly placeholders, and are flagged in-product.
Percentages at 60 months render directly and are never exponential-converted (mixture-cure family).
Response-rate endpoints display with a RESPONSE label and never participate in top ranking.
